literal: Even if you incur the enmity of those who plough with the bow, do not incur the enmity of those who plough with words.
translation: Even if you must brave the enmity of warriors who plough with the bow, never court the enmity of scholars and counselors who plough with words.
modern: வில்லை ஏராகக் கொண்ட வீரர்களின் பகையைப் பெற்றாலும், சொல்லை ஏராகக் கொண்ட அறிஞர்களின் பகையைப் பெறக் கூடாது.
explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful agricultural metaphor to compare physical power with intellectual power. Warriors are described as those who plough with the bow, using physical force to make their mark. Scholars, diplomats, and counselors are described as those who plough with words, using intellect and communication. The poet warns that while physical warfare is dangerous, the strategic and lasting damage caused by the enmity of wise and eloquent thinkers is far more destructive and impossible to overcome.
